t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup styled as an editorial magazine spread. The left third is a deep navy panel, the rest warm limestone. An oversized light-weight grotesk headline in three tight lines is cropped by the top edge and crosses the seam, limestone on navy and navy on limestone. Upper right: a framed hairline line drawing of a tangled double-line pipe knot with a few steel-blue segments. Along the bottom, five columns of slash-numbered monospace step labels and short sans text for <CONTENT>, split by hairline vertical rules, the first on navy. Flat, square, calm.
signature_idea: A giant cropped headline straddles a navy/limestone seam, inverting colour as it crosses, above a five-step response strip led by a call line.
strengths: strong, memorable editorial drama with light-weight type, on palette
colour inversion across the seam is a buildable CSS idea
five steps are clear and scannable with mono labels
pipe knot is a fitting metaphor for a fault
weaknesses: headline is so large it crowds the figure and pushes steps to a thin band
pipe knot has rounded generic bends, reads as decoration rather than a PP system
invented phone number and response times would be mistaken for real figures
step text is small; columns uneven in height
brand_fit_why: Navy, limestone, steel-blue accent, light headline and mono labels fit closely; the overscaled crop and decorative knot trade some calm for drama.
